name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+15 partisan lean
Incumbent Houchin has a massive financial advantage ($1.2M cash vs $18K)
Prediction markets price Houchin at ~95% to win
No polls or expert ratings; challenger Meyer is minimally funded
model.rationale: Houchin runs in an R+15 district with a huge fundraising edge and no meaningful outside spending against her, while markets price her near-certain. With no polls or ratings to the contrary, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly R+16 stands.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing Meyer competitive would be the only realistic path to moving this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Erin Houchin seeks a third term in a southern Indiana district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. She enters the general election with roughly $1.2 million on hand after raising nearly $1.9 million, while Democratic nominee Brad Meyer has raised about $105,000 with under $20,000 remaining. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is minimally funded.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Houchin about a 95% chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap points to a comfortable Republican win, with limited evidence suggesting the race could tighten.
